samples.summary: Workspace deletion and member removal bypass the new offline purge, leaving local document copies after access is gone
samples.evidence:
The change adds `purgeOfflineDocuments` to `deleteDocument` (packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts:167) and `deleteDocuments` (:215) on the stated rule that "content must not outlive the authority to read it" — which `docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:215` states as "Document deleted, **or workspace access lost** | Drop that entry". Two other frontend entry points reach exactly that outcome and do not purge:

- `deleteWorkspace(id)` — packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:88. `Document.workspace` is `onDelete: Cascade` (packages/backend/prisma/schema.prisma:125-126), so deleting a workspace deletes every document in it server-side while every locally persisted snapshot/changelog for those documents stays in IndexedDB until the 30-day sweep.
- `removeMember(...)` — packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:98. The removed member loses read authority for every document in that workspace; their on-disk copies remain.

A repo-wide grep shows `purgeOfflineDocuments` has exactly two call sites, both in `api/documents.ts`.

samples.summary: logout()'s new erase is a no-op on any route where PrivateRoute never mounted, so signing out can leave document content on a shared device
samples.evidence: `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` (packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-erase.ts:65) erases nothing unless module state `signedInUserId` was set, and the only writer is `rememberOfflineUser(userId)` in `OfflineRuntime` (packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx:42), mounted solely by `PrivateRoute`. `logout()` is also reached from `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 arm at packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:229, which runs on every authenticated request from routes registered *outside* `PrivateRoute` — `/shared/:token`, `/t/:id`, `/templates`, `/harness/*` (packages/frontend/src/App.tsx:107-127). A user who enabled offline persistence and wrote entries in an earlier session, then opens a share link directly in a fresh tab and has the session expire there, is signed out with `signedInUserId === undefined` and every stored snapshot left on disk — the exact case the per-device setting exists to protect. The fix belongs on the new code (record the identity from a place that covers every authenticated route, or derive it in `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout`).

samples.summary: The design-sandbox's @yorkie-js/react substitute documents (and relies on) an invariant this change falsifies: nothing called useYorkie, and YorkieProvider took no store/clientKey
samples.evidence: `packages/design-sandbox/src/scenes/canvas/yorkie-offline.tsx:82-97` states "A repo-wide grep of every `@yorkie-js/react` import in `packages/frontend/src` turns up exactly four runtime symbols in use... Nothing in scope calls `useRoot`, `useConnection`, `useRevisions`, `useRemoveDocument`, `useYorkie`, or `useYorkieDoc` — those pass through via `export *` as the REAL implementations... If anything ever calls one, it throws". This change adds `useYorkie()` in `LockRefusalWatch` (packages/frontend/src/components/durable-yorkie-provider.tsx) and a second `YorkieProvider` mount carrying `clientKey`/`store`, both inside `CollabDocumentProvider`, which is what the canvas scenes `sheet-editor`/`docs-editor`/`note-editor` render (packages/design-sandbox/scenes.config.json:235-260). It is inert only because `supportsClientKey()` is false at the pinned `@yorkie-js/react@0.7.22` (packages/frontend/package.json:65); the moment that pin is bumped — which the new code advertises as "the only action needed to turn the feature on" — the sandbox's pass-through `YorkieProvider` (line 204) silently drops `store`/`clientKey` and the real `useYorkie()` throws "must be used within a DocumentProvider" in the canvas scenes.

samples.summary: New always-loaded production modules value-import @yorkie-js/sdk, which packages/frontend lists only as a devDependency
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-copy.ts:1` (`import { Document } from "@yorkie-js/sdk"`) and `packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-copy-recovery.ts:1` (`import { Client, Document, Text }`) are runtime value imports, and they are now on the authenticated app's static path: `PrivateRoute.tsx` → `components/offline-runtime.tsx:8` → `lib/offline-copy`. `@yorkie-js/sdk` is declared at packages/frontend/package.json:97 under `devDependencies`, not `dependencies` (`@yorkie-js/react` is the runtime pin, line 65). It resolves today only because the workspace install hoists it (the same latitude `components/history/snapshot-adapters.ts:1` already takes), so nothing breaks in CI — but a production-only install would fail, and pulling the standalone SDK copy into the PrivateRoute entry path duplicates the ~857 KB copy `@yorkie-js/react` already bundles, against the enforced per-chunk budgets.

finding.summary: Workspace deletion and member removal bypass the new offline purge, leaving local document copies after access is gone
finding.evidence:
The change adds `purgeOfflineDocuments` to `deleteDocument` (packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts:167) and `deleteDocuments` (:215) on the stated rule that "content must not outlive the authority to read it" — which `docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:215` states as "Document deleted, **or workspace access lost** | Drop that entry". Two other frontend entry points reach exactly that outcome and do not purge:

- `deleteWorkspace(id)` — packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:88. `Document.workspace` is `onDelete: Cascade` (packages/backend/prisma/schema.prisma:125-126), so deleting a workspace deletes every document in it server-side while every locally persisted snapshot/changelog for those documents stays in IndexedDB until the 30-day sweep.
- `removeMember(...)` — packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:98. The removed member loses read authority for every document in that workspace; their on-disk copies remain.

A repo-wide grep shows `purgeOfflineDocuments` has exactly two call sites, both in `api/documents.ts`.

verdict.reason: The absence is real. `purgeOfflineDocuments` (packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-erase.ts:92) has exactly two production call sites, both in packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts (:167, :215). `deleteWorkspace` (packages/frontend/src/api/workspaces.ts:88) and `removeMember` (:98) perform the DELETE and return with no offline cleanup, and their UI callers (packages/frontend/src/app/workspaces/workspace-settings.tsx:132-141, :181-197) only invalidate queries, navigate and toast. I looked for an indirect path and found none: the only other store-deletion consumers are `dropAllForUser` on logout/preference-off (offline-erase.ts:30,73,161) and the age-based `collectStale()` sweep (packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx:69), which performs no access reconciliation; a repo-wide grep for `purge` across frontend .ts/.tsx turns up only the definitions in offline-erase.ts and wafflebase-doc-store.ts. The contract is stated in-repo: docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:215 ("Document deleted, or workspace access lost | Drop that entry") and packages/frontend/src/lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts:726,744-746 which documents purge/purgeDocument as serving exactly that row. Deleting a workspace cascades document deletion server-side while the same signed-in user's snapshots and change logs stay on disk until the 30-day sweep — content outliving the authority to read it, on a reachable path. Blast-radius lane fits: a cleanup invariant the new code establishes at one entry point is reachable at another entry point that does not pass through it. Severity major (the removeMember half is weaker, since the caller is usually the owner rather than the removed user, but self-removal is supported per packages/backend/src/workspace/workspace.service.spec.ts:342, and the deleteWorkspace half stands alone).

finding.summary: logout()'s new erase is a no-op on any route where PrivateRoute never mounted, so signing out can leave document content on a shared device
finding.evidence: `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` (packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-erase.ts:65) erases nothing unless module state `signedInUserId` was set, and the only writer is `rememberOfflineUser(userId)` in `OfflineRuntime` (packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx:42), mounted solely by `PrivateRoute`. `logout()` is also reached from `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 arm at packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:229, which runs on every authenticated request from routes registered *outside* `PrivateRoute` — `/shared/:token`, `/t/:id`, `/templates`, `/harness/*` (packages/frontend/src/App.tsx:107-127). A user who enabled offline persistence and wrote entries in an earlier session, then opens a share link directly in a fresh tab and has the session expire there, is signed out with `signedInUserId === undefined` and every stored snapshot left on disk — the exact case the per-device setting exists to protect. The fix belongs on the new code (record the identity from a place that covers every authenticated route, or derive it in `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout`).

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out. eraseOfflineDataOnLogout (offline-erase.ts:65-70) no-ops unless signedInUserId is set; the sole non-test writer is rememberOfflineUser in OfflineRuntime (offline-runtime.tsx:42), and OfflineRuntime is mounted only by PrivateRoute (PrivateRoute.tsx:35). logout() (auth.ts:105) is reached from fetchWithAuth's 401 arm (auth.ts:229), which runs for authenticated requests issued from routes registered outside PrivateRoute (App.tsx:110-127: /harness/*, /shared/:token, /t/:id, /templates, /). A concrete reachable bypass exists: template-landing.tsx:110 calls createFromTemplate through fetchWithAuth from the public /t/:id route (its own comment at :114 documents the 401 -> logout -> /login path), so a session expiring in a fresh tab on that route signs the user out with signedInUserId undefined and leaves every locally stored document snapshot on the device — precisely what the per-device setting and the erase-on-logout step exist to prevent. No other guard covers it; the only fallback is the thirty-day collectStale sweep, which also lives inside OfflineRuntime (offline-runtime.tsx:69). In-lane (entry point reaching a new cleanup without its precondition, visible only outside the diff) and major: silently skipped cleanup leaving document content on a shared device.

finding.summary: CollabDocumentProvider now calls fetchMe unconditionally, and it is mounted on the anonymous share-link route — a 401 there triggers logout() + hard redirect to /login
finding.evidence: `CollabDocumentProvider` gained `useQuery({queryKey:['me'], queryFn: fetchMe, retry:false})` (packages/frontend/src/components/collab-document-provider.tsx:152-156). It is rendered on the PUBLIC share route at packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:979, 998, 1007, 1022, 1035 (and, for shared PDFs, via `PdfCollabProvider` at packages/frontend/src/app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:199). `fetchMe` goes through `fetchWithAuth`, which on a 401 whose refresh fails calls `logout({redirect:false,...})` and then `redirectTo("/login")` — `window.location.href = '/login'` (packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:213-227). That route deliberately uses `fetchMeOptional` with key `['me','optional']` (shared-document.tsx:900-904) precisely to avoid this. An anonymous share-link visitor is now bounced to the login page. Fix belongs on the new code: use `fetchMeOptional` / the existing `['me','optional']` query, or skip the query outside PrivateRoute.

verdict.reason: The claimed code does not exist. `CollabDocumentProvider` calls `useQuery({queryKey:['me','optional'], queryFn: fetchMeOptional, retry:false})` at packages/frontend/src/components/collab-document-provider.tsx:165-169, and `fetchMe` is not imported in that file (only `fetchMeOptional, fetchYorkieToken` at line 5). The lines the reviewer cited (152-156) are a JSDoc paragraph that states the opposite of the claim — it explains that the component asks with `fetchMeOptional`, "never `fetchMe`", precisely because of the anonymous share route and `fetchWithAuth`'s 401 logout/redirect arm. The reviewer read the hazard described in the comment as the code. Furthermore `fetchMeOptional` (packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:144-170) uses bare `fetch`, not `fetchWithAuth`, and returns null on 401, so it cannot reach `logout()`/`redirectTo('/login')`; only `fetchMe` (auth.ts:124-138) goes through `fetchWithAuth`. The query key `['me','optional']` is identical to the one the public share route already uses (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:902-903), so the share route mounts (shared-document.tsx:992,1011,1020,1035,1048) and the shared-PDF path via PdfCollabProvider (packages/frontend/src/app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:199) share a cache entry and trigger no anonymous-visitor redirect. The prescribed fix is already the implemented state.

finding.summary: LossWatch calls useDocument() above the DocumentProvider it is meant to watch, so expectLoss can never latch in the real tree
finding.evidence: `DurableYorkieProvider` renders `<LockRefusalWatch><LossWatch store={store}>{children}</LossWatch></LockRefusalWatch>` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:98-100), and `children` here is the `inner` element that CONTAINS the `DocumentProvider` (collab-document-provider.tsx:160-165, 206). `LossWatch` therefore calls `useDocument()` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:120) outside any `DocumentProvider`, so it either throws or yields no doc, and `store.expectLoss(...)` is never called. Per the store's own contract that is exactly the failure it warns about: `remove` is called on every ordinary detach, so without the latch nothing is archived on real losses (packages/frontend/src/lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts `expectLoss` docs). The new test hides this because `useDocument` is mocked to return a doc regardless of provider nesting (packages/frontend/src/components/__tests__/collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:34-44).

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist in this repository. (1) `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:111-124` renders `<KeyedYorkieProvider><LockRefusalWatch><DurableDocumentScope value={value}>{children}</DurableDocumentScope></LockRefusalWatch></KeyedYorkieProvider>` — there is no `LossWatch store={store}` wrapper around children; a repo-wide grep for `LossWatch` finds only `DurableLossWatch`, defined at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:149 with exactly one render site. (2) That single render site is `collab-document-provider.tsx:183`, which is INSIDE the `DocumentProvider` opened at collab-document-provider.tsx:177 and closed at 185 — so `useDocument()` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:151) is called below the provider it needs, not above it. The store reaches it via context instead (`useDurableDocumentContext()` at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:150, provider `DurableDocumentScope` at durable-document-context.ts:45-53, mounted at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:121), which is what permits the component to sit where its hook works. The claimed line numbers do not match: line 120 is `<LockRefusalWatch onLockRefused={onLockRefused}>`, not a `useDocument()` call. (3) The claim that the test masks the bug is also false: the mock is provider-scoped — `useDocument: () => React.useContext(DocContext) ?? { doc: undefined }` at collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:62, with `DocumentProvider` supplying the context at lines 52-53 — and there is an explicit regression test `'subscribes from inside the DocumentProvider, not above it'` at lines 253-263 asserting a subscriber is registered, which would fail under the arrangement the finding describes. Since `expectLoss` IS reachable on the real tree, the downstream consequence (nothing archived on real losses) does not follow.
